# st-utilities_aes256_gcm_encrypt (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
# Generate the secret key and nonce as ephemeral values so they are never
# written to state or plan files. Requires the random provider >= 3.7.0 and
# Terraform >= 1.11 (write-only arguments and ephemeral resources).
# The .hex outputs are only the transport encoding (random raw bytes cannot
# be a Terraform string): the provider hex-decodes them and uses the raw bytes
# they represent -- the 32-byte AES-256 key and the 12-byte GCM nonce.

resource "random_bytes" "key" {
  length = 32
}

ephemeral "random_bytes" "nonce" {
  length = 12
}

resource "st-utilities_aes256_gcm_encrypt" "encrypt" {
  secret_key   = random_bytes.key.hex
  nonce        = ephemeral.random_bytes.nonce.hex
  string_value = jsonencode({ foo = "bar" })
  version      = 1
}

output "encrypted" {
  value     = st-utilities_aes256_gcm_encrypt.encrypt.encrypted_string_output
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `nonce` (String) Hex-encoded nonce/IV for AES-256-GCM. The value is hex-decoded and the resulting raw bytes are used directly as the GCM nonce, so it must decode to exactly 12 bytes -- the standard 96-bit GCM nonce (exactly 24 hexadecimal characters). A unique nonce must be used for every encryption with the same key -- nonce reuse with the same key is catastrophic for GCM. Recommended source: the random_bytes ephemeral resource (length = 12), passing its .hex output (24 hexadecimal characters, which the provider hex-decodes to the 12 generated bytes and uses as the nonce). Write-only: the value is only sent during create/update and is never stored in state or the plan file, so ephemeral values are accepted.
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive) Hex-encoded 32-byte (256-bit) key used for AES-256-GCM encryption. Must be exactly 64 hexadecimal characters (e.g. 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef). Write-only: the value is only sent during create/update and is never stored in state or the plan file, so ephemeral values (e.g. ephemeral "random_bytes" with length = 32, passing its .hex output) are accepted.
- `string_value` (String) The value to be encrypted. This can be either a JSON string (which will be minified and trimmed before encryption) or a plain string (which will be trimmed before encryption).

### Optional

- `additional_authenticated_data` (String) Optional additional data to authenticate but not encrypt. The same value must be provided when decrypting. If the AAD is tampered with, decryption will fail.
- `version` (Number) Version of the encryption inputs, used to trigger re-encryption when rotating the write-only secret_key and/or nonce. Write-only attribute values (secret_key, nonce) are never stored in state or plan files, so Terraform cannot detect when they change and no update would be planned -- the resource would keep the stale encrypted_string_output. Because this attribute IS stored in state, changing it (e.g. bumping 1 -> 2) produces a detectable diff that triggers an in-place update, during which string_value is re-encrypted with the freshly supplied secret_key and nonce from the configuration. Bump this version whenever the secret_key or nonce is rotated.

### Read-Only

- `encrypted_string_output` (String, Sensitive) JSON object containing the hex-encoded nonce (echoed exactly as provided, i.e. the hex encoding of the raw nonce bytes), base64-encoded ciphertext (includes auth tag), and the raw (unencoded) additional authenticated data (AAD).
